text:
Predicates:
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Invertebrate(x) ::: x is an invertebrate.
Vertebrate(x) ::: x is a vertebrate.
Backbone(x) ::: x has a backbone.
ReproduceByMating(x) ::: x reproduces by male-and-female mating.
Bee(x) ::: x is a bee.
QueenBee(x) ::: x is a queen bee.
Harry ::: Harry.

Premises:
∀x (Animal(x) → (Invertebrate(x) ∨ Vertebrate(x))) ::: Animals are either invertebrates or vertebrates.
∀x ((Animal(x) ∧ Backbone(x)) → ReproduceByMating(x)) ::: All animals with backbones reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (Vertebrate(x) → Backbone(x)) ::: All vertebrate animals have a backbone.
∀x (Bee(x) → ¬ReproduceByMating(x)) ::: All bees do not reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (QueenBee(x) → Bee(x)) ::: All queen bees are bees.
Bee(Harry) ::: Harry is a bee.

Conclusion:
Invertebrate(Harry) ∨ QueenBee(Harry) ::: Harry is an invertebrate or a queen bee.
